en.case.genebook.overview.label: Overview
en.case.genebook.overview.body: Marking the 10th anniversary of Health GeneTech Corp., a leader in Taiwan's biotechnology sector, I led a comprehensive 4-month rebranding initiative. As Lead Product Designer, I managed the end-to-end transformation of the Corporate Identity (CI) and official website — shifting the brand from a traditional "B2B lab" image to a professional yet vibrant "human-centric health partner".
en.case.genebook.problem.label: Problem
en.case.genebook.problem.headline: A 10-year-old brand stuck in "B2B lab" territory, inaccessible to the modern health-conscious consumer.
en.case.genebook.problem.challenge.label: Brand Challenge
en.case.genebook.problem.challenge.body: Health GeneTech's existing identity relied on cold, clinical visuals that resonated with lab partners but alienated the general public. The brand needed to communicate trust, modernity, and accessibility simultaneously — without losing scientific credibility. Additionally, professional medical terminology (e.g., "NGS") was intimidating and meaningless to everyday users.
en.case.genebook.insight.label: Key Strategic Insight
en.case.genebook.insight.body: During external testing, I discovered that translating "high-tech" into "high-value" — by highlighting the market value and premium pricing of equipment — immediately built user trust, even for those with no medical background.
en.case.genebook.process.label: Process
en.case.genebook.process.headline: Discovery → Architecture → Validation → Strategic Refinement.
en.case.genebook.process.01.name: Discovery
en.case.genebook.process.01.desc: Stakeholder interviews to define the "Why" behind the rebrand. Competitive analysis to identify market gaps and differentiation opportunities.
en.case.genebook.process.02.name: Architecture
en.case.genebook.process.02.desc: Established a clear Information Architecture to simplify complex genomic services. Internal usability testing refined the navigation bar and simplified "Instructional Steps".
en.case.genebook.process.03.name: Hi-Fi Design
en.case.genebook.process.03.desc: Integrated the new CI into a high-fidelity web interface. External usability testing with potential users validated the interface and surfaced the key trust insight.
en.case.genebook.process.04.name: Strategic Refinement
en.case.genebook.process.04.desc: Moved beyond technical jargon to strategically highlight market value — translating complex science into perceived quality and building immediate user trust.
en.case.genebook.solution.label: Solution
en.case.genebook.solution.headline: Morse Code as DNA metaphor — repositioning the brand as a "Biotechnological Decryptor".
en.case.genebook.solution.identity.label: Brand Identity
en.case.genebook.solution.identity.body: I replaced the outdated human-shaped trademark with a sophisticated logo inspired by Morse Code — symbolising that while DNA is the "source code" of life, Health GeneTech acts as the expert "decoder." I departed from conventional biotech blues and greens, selecting Vibrant Orange and Professional Red as the primary palette, injecting energy and approachability into the brand.
en.case.genebook.solution.system.label: Systemisation
en.case.genebook.solution.system.body: To ensure long-term scalability, I delivered a complete CI Brand Manual covering logotype standards, a 12-column grid system, and unified design components — making the system handoff-ready from day one.
en.case.genebook.impact.label: of users value quality content over price
en.case.genebook.impact.desc: Qualitative research confirmed that clear diagrams presenting the testing process were the most effective trust-building mechanism — guiding the final information hierarchy.
en.case.genebook.outcome.label: Outcome
en.case.genebook.outcome.headline: A holistic brand transformation — scientific rigour meets human warmth.
en.case.genebook.outcome.strategic.title: Strategic Design & Branding
en.case.genebook.outcome.strategic.1: Holistic Transformation: Successfully integrated graphic design, UI design, and CI to revitalise a premier Taiwanese biotechnology company.
en.case.genebook.outcome.strategic.2: Narrative Identity: Morse code repositioned the brand as a "Biotechnological Decryptor."
en.case.genebook.outcome.strategic.3: Emotional Connectivity: Transitioned from cold clinical tones to a vibrant, youthful palette.
en.case.genebook.outcome.strategic.4: Systemic Scalability: Delivered a rigorous CI manual with logotypes, 12-column grid, and typography standards.
en.case.genebook.outcome.ux.title: User-Centric UX Insights
en.case.genebook.outcome.ux.1: Trust Through Transparency: Highlighting equipment market value bridged the knowledge gap for laypeople.
en.case.genebook.outcome.ux.2: Intuitive IA: Refined navigation bar and simplified instructional steps for complex genomic information.
en.case.genebook.outcome.ux.3: Actionable Data: 80% of users value high-quality content over price — reinforcing the need for clear process diagrams.

en.case.tfl.overview.label: Overview
en.case.tfl.overview.body: Despite a saturated fitness app market, high churn rates persist. Most apps fail by burdening users with complex data entry during intense workouts. My goal was to design a frictionless tracking system that maintains training momentum and boosts long-term engagement — transforming the solitary nature of working out into a vibrant, human-centred experience.
en.case.tfl.strategy.label: Strategy
en.case.tfl.strategy.headline: Triple W framework — Why, How, What — to ensure every decision is user-grounded.
en.case.tfl.strategy.01.name: Audit
en.case.tfl.strategy.01.desc: Conducted competitive analysis to identify navigation bottlenecks in top-tier fitness apps. Existing apps lack trainer follow-up and community features.
en.case.tfl.strategy.02.name: Design
en.case.tfl.strategy.02.desc: Implemented gesture-based navigation and predictive data entry to minimise cognitive load during workouts. IA and Task Flows served as the blueprint for the Deliver phase.
en.case.tfl.strategy.03.name: Validate
en.case.tfl.strategy.03.desc: Executed usability testing with 5 active lifters to measure task completion speed and flow satisfaction. Design Review phase synthesised post-interview feedback with engineering feasibility.
en.case.tfl.design.label: Design
en.case.tfl.design.headline: Bridging expert guidance with social connectivity — beyond just tracking numbers.
en.case.tfl.design.scalability.label: Scalability
en.case.tfl.design.scalability.body: Developed a comprehensive Design System to ensure visual consistency and 2× faster developer handoff. A Design Review phase synthesised feedback from user post-interviews and technical feasibility assessments before the final Deliver stage.
en.case.tfl.conclusion.label: Conclusion
en.case.tfl.conclusion.body: "Beyond Tracking: Elevating the Fitness Journey through Connection and Insight."

en.case.vcue.hero.title: Visual Cues Study
en.case.vcue.hero.subtitle: How visual cues in fitness instructional videos affect beginner motor learning — a three-phase mixed-methods study producing an original design framework.
en.case.vcue.meta.role.label: Role
en.case.vcue.meta.institution.label: Institution
en.case.vcue.meta.duration.label: Duration
en.case.vcue.meta.methods.label: Methods
en.case.vcue.overview.label: Overview
en.case.vcue.overview.body: This study investigates how visual cues in fitness instructional videos affect beginners' motor learning. Through a three-phase approach, I evaluated four types of visual cues — directional, measurement, body highlight, and metaphor — across quantitative performance data and qualitative user insights. The study produced an original design framework: the Dynamic Balance Model of Cognitive Load and Learning Effectiveness.
en.case.vcue.gap.label: Research Gap
en.case.vcue.gap.headline: 86% of people use video to learn physical skills. Almost no one has studied whether those videos actually work.
en.case.vcue.gap.problem.label: The Problem
en.case.vcue.gap.problem.body: Digital learning has fundamentally changed how beginners approach physical training. Over 70% of users turn to YouTube to learn exercises like squats and stretching. Yet without professional guidance, learners routinely imitate incorrectly — leading to poor form and risk of injury. The deeper problem is systemic: the design of visual cues in existing tutorial videos is driven by intuition and aesthetic preference, not evidence. There are no established guidelines for what works.
en.case.vcue.gap.context.label: Research Context
en.case.vcue.gap.context.body: Prior research has focused on VR/AR and interactive systems, leaving video-based motor learning systematically underexplored. This study addresses that gap by examining four cue types through the lens of Cognitive Load Theory and the theory of external attention.
en.case.vcue.question.label: Research Question
en.case.vcue.question.body: How do four types of visual cues — directional, measurement, body highlighting, and metaphorical — support and improve beginner motor learning in instructional videos?
en.case.vcue.methodology.label: Methodology
en.case.vcue.methodology.headline: A three-phase mixed-methods approach — quantitative and qualitative, beginners and experts.
en.case.vcue.methodology.survey.name: Online Survey
en.case.vcue.methodology.survey.body: Distributed to fitness beginners aged 18–40 via social media and university networks. The survey mapped learning habits, video-watching behaviour, and initial preferences for six types of visual cues — including skeletal overlays and muscle activation highlights. Participant feedback identified four cue types as the focus for subsequent testing.
en.case.vcue.methodology.usability.name: Usability Testing
en.case.vcue.methodology.usability.body: Each participant watched four short squat tutorial videos, each embedding a different visual cue type. Performance was observed and recorded. Post-task interviews collected qualitative insights on clarity, helpfulness, and perceived cognitive load. A counterbalanced design controlled for order effects.
en.case.vcue.methodology.expert.name: Expert Evaluation
en.case.vcue.methodology.expert.body: Coaches, personal trainers, and experienced exercisers evaluated an optimised video integrating all four cue types. This phase gathered professional validation and critical perspective, allowing cross-comparison between novice and expert responses — which revealed significant differences in how cues are perceived across experience levels.
en.case.vcue.premise.label: Core Premise
en.case.vcue.premise.body: Most instructional video designs are built on intuition and aesthetic preference, not evidence. This study produced a systematic ranking of the four cue types for beginner motor learning in instructional fitness videos — grounding design decisions in observed data rather than assumption.
en.case.vcue.experiment.label: The Experiment
en.case.vcue.experiment.headline: Four cue types. One squat. Measured against the same beginners, under the same conditions.
en.case.vcue.experiment.directional.name: Directional Cues
en.case.vcue.experiment.directional.def: Arrows and motion lines that indicate the direction and path of movement. Immediately communicates where the body should go, reducing ambiguity about force and trajectory.
en.case.vcue.experiment.highlight.name: Body Highlight Cues
en.case.vcue.experiment.highlight.def: Glow or colour emphasis on specific muscle groups or joints during movement. Draws attention to where activation should occur, supporting body awareness and proprioception.
en.case.vcue.experiment.metaphor.name: Metaphor Cues
en.case.vcue.experiment.metaphor.def: Life-like comparisons that translate abstract movement concepts into familiar imagery — e.g. "sit back into an invisible chair." Relies on prior experience to be decoded correctly.
en.case.vcue.experiment.measurement.name: Measurement Cues
en.case.vcue.experiment.measurement.def: Angle lines, degree markers, and depth indicators overlaid on the body. Provides precise numerical reference but requires abstract interpretation that overwhelms beginners.
en.case.vcue.qual.label: Qualitative Findings
en.case.vcue.qual.headline: Gioia coding made the hierarchy visible: each cue has a different role — and a different cost for beginners.
en.case.vcue.qual.directional.name: Directional
en.case.vcue.qual.directional.body: Provides real-time movement guidance and corrective feedback. Participants found it immediately clear and lowest in cognitive cost — but weak contrast, missing motion, or poor timing could make the arrow feel like UI chrome rather than instruction.
en.case.vcue.qual.highlight.name: Body Highlight
en.case.vcue.qual.highlight.body: Directs attention to muscle activation and postural control. Useful when timed well; pacing and overuse emerged as key qualitative risks.
en.case.vcue.qual.metaphor.name: Metaphor
en.case.vcue.qual.metaphor.body: Conveys movement via analogy. Intuitive for participants with prior exercise experience — ambiguous and harder to embody for true beginners.
en.case.vcue.qual.measurement.name: Measurement
en.case.vcue.qual.measurement.body: Offers precision and standards, but abstract numbers are hard to translate into physical movement. High cognitive load with limited beginner payoff.
en.case.vcue.qual.cross.label: Cross-cutting
en.case.vcue.qual.cross.item1: Cues differ in function, not only preference rank: guidance vs. attention vs. analogy vs. precision.
en.case.vcue.qual.cross.item2: High precision ≠ beginner-usable: measurement's qualitative reception explains its weak quantitative standing.
en.case.vcue.qual.cross.item3: Design priorities from the coding: visual clarity first; then timing and pacing; avoid stacking too many cue types simultaneously.
en.case.vcue.qual.bridge.label: From coding to model
en.case.vcue.qual.bridge.body: Comparing these roles across the four coding trees — not researcher intuition alone — underpinned the Dynamic Balance Model (learning effectiveness × cognitive load). The quantitative scores in the next section align with these qualitative roles.
en.case.vcue.qual.method.label: Method
en.case.vcue.qual.method.body: Inductive Gioia coding (1st-order concepts → 2nd-order themes → aggregate dimensions) was applied to post-task interview transcripts from beginner usability testing. The analysis ran per cue, producing four comparable coding trees. Staying in participant language before theorising ensured the framework reflected what users said, not what was assumed.
en.case.vcue.qual.order1.title: 1st Order Concepts
en.case.vcue.qual.order1.desc: Raw participant quotes tagged with emergent descriptive codes — language stays close to the informant's own words
en.case.vcue.qual.order2.title: 2nd Order Themes
en.case.vcue.qual.order2.desc: 1st order codes grouped by conceptual similarity into researcher-identified theoretical categories
en.case.vcue.qual.order3.title: Aggregate Dimensions
en.case.vcue.qual.order3.desc: 2nd order themes consolidated into high-level theoretical constructs that explain the underlying phenomenon
en.case.vcue.gioia.dir.title: 01 — Directional Cues
en.case.vcue.gioia.dir.insight: Clear real-time guidance — but can be misread as UI chrome
en.case.vcue.gioia.hl.title: 02 — Body Highlight Cues
en.case.vcue.gioia.hl.insight: Focuses attention on form — pacing can overload
en.case.vcue.gioia.met.title: 03 — Metaphor Cues
en.case.vcue.gioia.met.insight: Relatable for some — ambiguous for true beginners
en.case.vcue.gioia.meas.title: 04 — Measurement Cues
en.case.vcue.gioia.meas.insight: Precise on paper — hard to embody; high load
en.case.vcue.findings.label: Findings
en.case.vcue.findings.headline: A clear hierarchy emerged. Not all visual cues help beginners equally.
en.case.vcue.findings.source.label: Data Source
en.case.vcue.findings.source.body: These scores align with the qualitative roles above. Scores are Likert mean ratings from post-condition self-report questionnaires (n=10 beginners, Iteration 01 usability testing). Each participant watched all four cue videos in counterbalanced order and rated each immediately after. Effectiveness summarises the Preference dimension from dissertation Table 2; Cognitive Load summarises the self-reported Mental Effort dimension. Full six-dimension data (Usefulness, Clarity, Distraction, Mental Effort, Engagement, Preference) with standard deviations are reported in dissertation Table 2.

en.case.vcue.findings.row2.name: Body Highlight Cues

en.case.vcue.vs.label: Beginners vs Experts
en.case.vcue.vs.headline: Experience changes everything. The same cue lands completely differently depending on who is watching.
en.case.vcue.vs.divergence.label: Key Divergence
en.case.vcue.vs.divergence.body: Expert evaluators rated metaphor cues significantly higher than beginners — because they already possess the conceptual framework to decode abstract comparisons. For beginners, the same cue created confusion. Measurement cues showed the opposite pattern: experts valued precision, but beginners were overwhelmed by numbers they couldn't contextualise into physical movement. This divergence confirms that visual cue design cannot be one-size-fits-all.
en.case.vcue.vs.dir.name: Directional
en.case.vcue.vs.dir.note: Agreement across groups — unanimously the clearest cue
en.case.vcue.vs.hl.name: Body Highlight
en.case.vcue.vs.hl.note: Experts more precise in feedback — noted timing and overuse risks
en.case.vcue.vs.met.name: Metaphor
en.case.vcue.vs.met.note: Experts found it intuitive and memorable; beginners found it ambiguous without context
en.case.vcue.vs.meas.name: Measurement
en.case.vcue.vs.meas.note: Experts valued precision; beginners were overwhelmed by numbers without physical reference
en.case.vcue.model.label: Original Framework
en.case.vcue.model.headline: The Dynamic Balance Model — plotting visual cues against the tension between learning effectiveness and cognitive cost.
en.case.vcue.model.theModel.label: The Model
en.case.vcue.model.theModel.body: This study's primary contribution is a two-axis framework for evaluating instructional visual cues. By mapping Learning Effectiveness against Cognitive Load, the model creates four zones — Optimal, Overload, Ineffective, and Confusing — that provide actionable guidance for video designers. The model also identifies the Double-Edged Sword Effect: integrating multiple cues simultaneously increases perceived professionalism but raises cognitive load, potentially undermining learning efficiency.
en.case.vcue.sword.label: Key Finding
en.case.vcue.sword.body: The Double-Edged Sword Effect: integrating multiple visual cues simultaneously enhances professionalism and trust — but raises cognitive load and may fragment focus, ultimately reducing overall learning efficiency.
en.case.vcue.principles.label: Design Principles
en.case.vcue.principles.headline: Eight evidence-based guidelines for instructional video creators.
en.case.vcue.principles.selection.title: Cue Selection
en.case.vcue.principles.selection.item1: Prioritise directional cues for clear and immediate movement guidance.
en.case.vcue.principles.selection.item2: Use body highlighting to focus on key body parts — but avoid overuse.
en.case.vcue.principles.selection.item3: Be cautious with measurement cues; numbers may confuse beginners.
en.case.vcue.principles.selection.item4: Apply metaphorical cues contextually — they work better for experienced learners.
en.case.vcue.principles.delivery.title: Delivery & Structure
en.case.vcue.principles.delivery.item1: Ensure timely appearance of cues at critical movement moments.
en.case.vcue.principles.delivery.item2: Keep videos short (~90 seconds) to match beginner attention and preference.
en.case.vcue.principles.delivery.item3: Do not display more than two cue types simultaneously — cognitive overload risk.
en.case.vcue.principles.delivery.item4: Incorporate multiple camera angles to reduce blind spots and support diverse learner needs.
en.case.vcue.reflection.label: Reflection
en.case.vcue.reflection.headline: What it means to design with evidence, not assumption.
en.case.vcue.reflection.researcher.label: As a Researcher
en.case.vcue.reflection.researcher.body: This project deepened my conviction that design decisions must be grounded in evidence. The multi-phase methodology — survey to usability testing to expert evaluation — showed me how much a single method misses, and how triangulation builds credibility. The Gioia coding process transformed raw participant quotes into a structured framework, revealing patterns invisible to intuition.
en.case.vcue.reflection.designer.label: As a Designer
en.case.vcue.reflection.designer.body: The most surprising finding was the experience gap: cues that experts found intuitive were actively confusing to beginners. This reinforced a principle I now carry into every design project — that your own familiarity with a system is the least reliable measure of its usability. Designing for someone who doesn't yet know what you know requires deliberate research, not empathy alone.
en.case.vcue.reflection.limitations.label: Limitations
en.case.vcue.reflection.limitations.body: The study has inherent constraints worth acknowledging. The sample sizes were small — 10 beginners for usability testing, 10 experts for evaluation — limiting statistical generalisability. The findings are based on a single movement (the squat), and may not transfer directly to other exercises or motor skill domains. Cognitive load was measured through self-report scales rather than physiological methods, introducing subjective bias. Additionally, the controlled research setting differs from real-world video consumption conditions. These constraints are common to early-stage exploratory research and point to productive directions for future work.
en.case.vcue.experiment.metaphor.verdict: Expert-first — Novices find harder to interpret

en.case.overheadflights.hero.role.label: Role
en.case.overheadflights.hero.focus.label: Focus
en.case.overheadflights.hero.platform.label: Platform

en.case.overheadflights.situation.label: Situation
en.case.overheadflights.situation.title: Mainstream apps all require you to actively open and search; the passive, single-device direction has already been done in hardware.
en.case.overheadflights.situation.market.p1: Most people spend the majority of their day glued to a phone or a laptop. This product starts from that observation: it connects a screen saver with real flight information, using the lowest possible amount of disruption to let someone feel a faint sense of connection to another person.
en.case.overheadflights.situation.market.p2: There's no shortage of plane-tracking tools — FlightRadar24, Plane Finder, FlightAware all lay the whole sky out as a map, a list, an alert feed. They require you to actively open the app to check; at their core, they're dashboards. The maker community has also built hardware for this: Airframe (a Raspberry Pi + e-paper display) quietly shows the nearest plane overhead — a gift its creator built for a friend who lived under a flight path. The idea itself is not something I thought of first.
en.case.overheadflights.situation.row2.limi: Requires buying parts, assembly, takes up physical space
en.case.overheadflights.situation.row3.limi: No flight information, or unrelated to flight
en.case.overheadflights.positioning.label: Positioning
en.case.overheadflights.positioning.title: The gap isn't the idea of "a plane overhead" — it's the intersection: a macOS screen saver.
en.case.overheadflights.positioning.body: After checking, the actual gap isn't the concept of "a plane overhead" — it's the intersection: a macOS screen saver × real flight data × editorial typography. Mainstream apps' business models don't encourage a passive screen saver; Airframe proves the passive, single-device direction works, but it adds a physical device. There's no direct precedent for a software screen saver doing this — the argument has to address Airframe head-on, not pretend the market is empty.
en.case.overheadflights.integrity.label: Data integrity
en.case.overheadflights.integrity.body: A portfolio mockup can look beautiful, but if the claim is "a plane overhead," the data has to be live ADS-B — not a faked callsign animation. The data source's terms of use (non-commercial / educational / personal) also had to be checked before writing them into the README.
en.case.overheadflights.task.label: Task
en.case.overheadflights.task.title: Take the real-time data that used to live only inside tracking apps, and move it into the screen saver that was already idle.
en.case.overheadflights.task.goal.label: Goal
en.case.overheadflights.task.goal.body: Move real-time data — the plane currently flying overhead, information that used to live only inside tracking apps — into the screen saver a computer is already running. No new app, no new device, no active searching: just replace what the screen saver shows, so a person can feel a faint human connection while being almost entirely undisturbed.
en.case.overheadflights.task.quote: “I decided to build a screensaver that quietly shows flight information, so people feel connected without any effort.”
en.case.overheadflights.task.role: Role: independently conceived and decided on direction, visuals, trade-offs, and risk. AI collaborated on research synthesis, drafting, and implementation — rules described below.
en.case.overheadflights.ai.label: Action · AI
en.case.overheadflights.ai.title: Four tools, each with its own job — I'm the gatekeeper at every step.
en.case.overheadflights.ai.collab.label: Collaboration
en.case.overheadflights.ai.collab.intro: This wasn't throwing one prompt at a tool and waiting for a result. Four tools, each with a distinct job, and I'm the gatekeeper at every step:
en.case.overheadflights.ai.claude.role: First-pass thinking: breaking down the problem, synthesizing market research, drafting the spec, early technical trade-offs
en.case.overheadflights.ai.perplexity.role: Verifying claims: finding primary documents and research to check whether claims in the market research and design rationale actually hold up
en.case.overheadflights.ai.grok.role: Only catches errors: doesn't redo the thinking; reviews facts, assumptions, risks
en.case.overheadflights.ai.cursor.role: Only executes task packages that have already passed review; doesn't improvise before review
en.case.overheadflights.ai.perplexity.why: The reason for choosing Perplexity is straightforward: general-purpose AI answers can occasionally sound authoritative while having no real source behind them. Perplexity attaches sources to its answers, which lets me go back and verify instead of taking it at face value. That matters for a portfolio argument that will actually be scrutinized — claims about "where the gap is" in the market research, and the research cited in the design rationale, both need to trace back to real documents, not just "the AI said so."
en.case.overheadflights.ai.gatekeeping.titl: Gatekeeping examples (this isn't a process demo — it's the judgment itself)
en.case.overheadflights.ai.gate.1: Perplexity's MCP tool kept returning 404 errors. I didn't wait for the tool to get fixed, and I didn't fill the gap with an AI's unverified memory — I opened a browser myself and manually verified the research instead. The judgment call: when a tool fails, there's a choice between "get something down now, verify later" and "just do it manually." I chose the latter, because this market research ultimately has to support the claim that "this gap is real" — it can't afford to rest on unverified information.
en.case.overheadflights.ai.gate.2: A draft wanted to state adsbdb's rate limit as a specific number. That number had never been verified against a primary source — it was just a plausible-sounding guess from the AI. I required that "no number goes in without primary-source verification," and changed it to conservative, verifiable language instead (phrasing like "well below the public 1 req/s limit" — checkable, but not overstated). The judgment call: a portfolio gets scrutinized, and an unsourced number is worse for credibility than no number at all.
en.case.overheadflights.ai.gate.3: The AI surfaced an unfavorable precedent: Airframe. The safer move would have been to avoid mentioning it and let readers assume the idea was original. I chose to address it directly instead: acknowledging that Airframe had already done the "nearest plane overhead" concept earlier, and narrowing the difference down to "form factor (screen saver vs. hardware) + execution (editorial typography vs. e-paper)." The judgment call: not finding a competitor doesn't mean you've won. Being willing to face the competitor you did find head-on is what actually demonstrates product judgment — not how thorough the market research was.
en.case.overheadflights.ai.gate.4: Once the visual design was finalized, I marked it frozen in the documentation. I told the AI explicitly: "the text size and layout are already right — don't touch them unless I say so" — and confined its remaining freedom to the data layer and background effects. The judgment call: AI has no built-in sense of "good enough, stop here" — left alone, it tends to keep micro-adjusting past the point of visible difference. Freezing the design was a line I drew deliberately; it wasn't something the AI converged on by itself.
en.case.overheadflights.ai.principle.label: Principle
en.case.overheadflights.ai.principle.body: AI accelerates drafts and implementation. Whether something passes is my decision.
en.case.overheadflights.research.label: Action · Research & Design
en.case.overheadflights.research.title: First verify whether the market gap is real, then decide which frameworks actually support "quiet."
en.case.overheadflights.research.step1: Define the problem itself first, before rushing to research tools. Is the actual gap the feature of "tracking planes," or the experience of "being able to passively notice something without actively checking"? Get the problem definition wrong, and no amount of competitor research afterward will fix it.
en.case.overheadflights.research.step2: Scan mainstream apps' product logic and delivery format (FlightRadar24, Plane Finder, FlightAware), and confirm their core assumption is "the user will actively open the app to check." That assumption itself is the actual limitation in the market structure — not just a descriptive word chosen at random.
en.case.overheadflights.research.step3: Go further and check maker projects, articles, and GitHub (Airframe, FlightTracker, etc.), deliberately looking for precedents unfavorable to my own claim, to avoid convincing myself the market was empty. This step exists so the positioning statement in the Situation section can survive the most direct rebuttal: "hasn't someone already done this?"
en.case.overheadflights.research.step4: Verify API terms against primary documentation (airplanes.live's rate limit, terms of use). Any number without a primary source doesn't go into a public-facing document — better to use conservative, verifiable language than a number that looks more precise but has no traceable source.
en.case.overheadflights.research.step5: Converge on a single positioning statement that can withstand challenge: acknowledge the precedent exists, and compress the actual difference down to two points — "the screen saver as the medium" + "editorial typography as the execution" — rather than vaguely claiming "nothing like this exists."
en.case.overheadflights.research.design.int: Three frameworks, one line each, then down to the actual numbers:
en.case.overheadflights.research.framework1: Calm technology (Weiser & Brown, 1995): Information stays at the periphery of attention, and only moves to the center when needed. The original paper's motivation was countering the anxiety caused by information overload — not just saving attention.
en.case.overheadflights.research.framework2: Soft fascination (attention restoration, Kaplan & Kaplan, 1989): Effortless, gentle stimulation (like watching clouds) lets attention rest after a long stretch of focus. That's the reason this product lives in the "idle / lock screen" moment — it's meant to serve a moment of rest, not add one more information source to process.
en.case.overheadflights.research.framework3: Ambient intimacy / social snacking (Reichelt, 2007; Gardner, Pickett & Knowles, 2005): Passive exposure to a symbol of another person's existence — even without any interaction — can lower feelings of isolation. A stranger's flight quietly appearing is a small signal that "someone else out there is moving through their life right now," almost like someone quietly checking in on you.
en.case.overheadflights.research.visual.tit: How these three frameworks became actual visual decisions:
en.case.overheadflights.research.visual.1: Arousal is driven by brightness and saturation, not hue (Valdez & Mehrabian, 1994) — this is the basis for the near-black background (rgb(0.02, 0.02, 0.025)) plus low-saturation silver-white text. There's no need to lean on the cliché of "cool colors" to create a sense of calm — lowering brightness and saturation directly is enough.
en.case.overheadflights.research.visual.2: The text hierarchy decays by proportional opacity, not equal steps: callsign 0.82 → airline 0.48 → meta 0.34 → monogram 0.28. This proportional decay matches the eye's non-linear perception of brightness differences (Weber-Fechner) — in a low-contrast environment, proportional steps make each level of hierarchy feel evenly spaced, instead of forcing hierarchy through harsh contrast.
en.case.overheadflights.research.visual.3: No cards, no borders, no icons — just a minimal stack of text (aesthetic-usability effect, Kurosu & Kashimura, 1995): people read visual restraint directly as "this thing won't bother me." For a product that appears during lock screen / idle moments, that's a hard requirement — the context of use itself demands "don't disturb."
en.case.overheadflights.research.visual.4: Motion only serves genuine information changes: a new flight fades in over ≤0.4 seconds; an update to the same flight has no animation at all; a slow, multi-minute 4–6px anti-burn-in drift; and it respects the system's "reduce motion" setting. In a low-arousal environment, any unnecessary motion reads as disruption — so it only moves when there's actually something new to show.
en.case.overheadflights.research.constraint: Hard constraint of the screen saver: any mouse movement or key press exits it immediately — there's no intermediate state like "click to reveal more." So disclosure is reduced to two honest states:
en.case.overheadflights.research.state.plan: Shows callsign, airline, altitude, bearing. As long as it stays within range, it keeps displaying (updated roughly every 90 seconds); only leaving range or losing the flight returns it to black.
en.case.overheadflights.research.interest: The interest comes from the rarity of the event itself (a real plane actually passing over), not from stacking interactions or animation to please. When data can't be fetched, it fails silently into black rather than showing an error — a quiet way to fail, and part of the same "don't disturb" principle.
en.case.overheadflights.data.label: Action · Data & Build
en.case.overheadflights.data.title: After three separate WebView failures, the whole architecture moved to native.
en.case.overheadflights.data.radius: Radius 40 km, an altitude threshold, and a 90-second polling interval — these three numbers are the result of a trade-off: too small a radius means long stretches of black (which feels broken); too large a radius shows planes that clearly aren't "overhead," undermining the product's core claim. The 90-second polling interval sits well below airplanes.live's public 1 req/s limit, trading a generous safety margin for stability — not having to worry about being rate-limited — at the cost of the data not being second-by-second real-time. But this product wants "a quiet environmental fact," not a tracking dashboard; second-level real-time was never the goal.
en.case.overheadflights.data.gps: Without GPS, it falls back to a fixed location (Wembley Park, London), documented as something the user can change themselves — not a hardcoded, unchangeable assumption.
en.case.overheadflights.data.callsigns: Multiple real callsigns verified against the API — this is the bottom line of the entire "plane overhead" claim: if the flight data were fake, the whole point of the project would break. What this product is meant to make someone feel is "a real stranger is genuinely flying overhead right now" — that connection has to be real, or it's just decoration. A portfolio mockup can look beautiful, but faking the data would make the claim itself collapse.
en.case.overheadflights.data.classification: Classification: non-commercial, portfolio use only; any rate-limit number without primary-source verification is stated conservatively rather than as a hard figure.
en.case.overheadflights.data.quote: “If the flight data were fake, the whole point of the project would break — the connection has to be real, or it's just decoration.”
en.case.overheadflights.data.pipeline: Location (or fallback) → airplanes.live (nearest plane, 90s polling) → (optional) adsbdb airline/route → macOS .saver URLSession for data · AppKit for text · Core Image for background → System Settings → Customize screen saver
en.case.overheadflights.data.webview.intro: The original approach handled everything through WebView (rendering, text, data requests), and it hit repeated failures inside the legacyScreenSaver environment, forcing the whole architecture to change direction:
en.case.overheadflights.data.webview.1: WebView's fetch was unreliable — the exact same code worked fine in a regular browser, but would silently fail inside the screen saver environment, with no clear error to catch. Fix: move all data requests to native NSURLSession.
en.case.overheadflights.data.webview.2: WebView's text animation would freeze — requestAnimationFrame and opacity transitions would lock up in this environment, causing the text fade-in to simply fail. Fix: render text with native AppKit NSTextField, and let AppKit's own animation handle the motion.
en.case.overheadflights.data.webview.3: WebView's background frequently failed to render at all — the whole screen would occasionally show up blank, with the background layer not painting. Fix: render the background with native Core Image (Etheral Shadow style: grayscale mask + distortion + noise).
en.case.overheadflights.data.webview.conclu: The conclusion from all three failures was a dual-layer native approach: AppKit for text, Core Image for the background, URLSession for data — WebView dropped out of the main path entirely. The cost of this decision was losing the flexibility of iterating quickly with web technology; what it bought instead was genuine stability inside the screen saver environment. It only replaces the screen saver's content — it doesn't change the wait time a user sets in System Settings.
en.case.overheadflights.ship.label: Action · Ship
en.case.overheadflights.ship.title: The project has to be something a friend can actually install — not something that only runs on my own Mac.
en.case.overheadflights.ship.delivery.label: Delivery
en.case.overheadflights.ship.github: GitHub public: rowanlin801229/overhead-flights — chosen to be public rather than shared privately, because the portfolio's claim is "this data is real," and making the source public lets that claim actually be checked, rather than just asserted.
en.case.overheadflights.ship.script: macos/build-and-install.sh: a one-command build-and-install script, designed for "a friend who has Xcode but doesn't know this project's internals" — not an internal tool only I can understand.
en.case.overheadflights.ship.readme: Three-step README + Gatekeeper handling: since the project isn't signed by a developer account, macOS blocks unsigned software by default, so the README has to spell out exactly how to get past the Gatekeeper warning — it can't assume the user already knows how to handle it.
en.case.overheadflights.ship.assets: Portfolio assets: the main mockup image, overhead-flights-demo.mp4 (an actual capture of BAW8RM, a flight with a fully resolved route), and a static hero image — chosen because it shows callsign, airline, origin → destination, and altitude/bearing all at once, all real data, not layout placeholders.
en.case.overheadflights.result.label: Result
en.case.overheadflights.result.title: A quiet ambient display, not a dashboard.
en.case.overheadflights.result.outcome.body: A quiet ambient display: it doesn't compete for attention by interrupting. When a plane is present, it gives a restrained cue; when it isn't, it's just black. It turns "there's a plane overhead" into an environmental fact that can be noticed, never forced on anyone.
en.case.overheadflights.result.row2.result: ✅ Multiple real callsigns, verifiable against airplanes.live
en.case.overheadflights.result.row3.goal: Polling respects the spirit of the public terms
en.case.overheadflights.result.row3.result: ✅ 90-second polling, below the official 1 req/s limit
en.case.overheadflights.result.row4.goal: Visuals read as editorial typography, not a tracking tool
en.case.overheadflights.result.row4.result: ✅ Near-black background + AppKit text; no map, no list, no terminal green
en.case.overheadflights.result.row5.goal: A third person can install it from the docs
en.case.overheadflights.result.row5.result: ⚠️ README and script are ready; no friend test-install feedback yet
en.case.overheadflights.result.row6.result: ✅ Airframe addressed directly; the difference distilled to medium + aesthetic execution
en.case.overheadflights.result.limitations: Limitations: Unsigned, so it triggers Gatekeeper; falls back to a fixed location without GPS; macOS only; adsbdb's exact rate limit has no primary-source number, so the wording stays conservative.
en.case.overheadflights.result.learned.1: An unfamiliar runtime environment (legacyScreenSaver) can't be assumed to behave like a normal web stack — technical validation should happen earlier.
en.case.overheadflights.result.learned.2: Not finding a direct competitor doesn't mean you've won. Finding Airframe and still being willing to address it head-on, with an argument that holds up — that's what product judgment actually looks like.

en.case.faintv.situation.label: S — Situation
en.case.faintv.situation.title: A TV streaming service where elderly users couldn't complete basic tasks on their own.
en.case.faintv.situation.body: FainTV is a Taiwanese TV streaming service. Its core audience watches on a shared living-room screen — many are elderly users who rely on a remote control as their primary input device.
en.case.faintv.situation.challenge1: Remote-control text input is slow and exhausting — especially for elderly users trying to search for content or log in.
en.case.faintv.situation.challenge2: A voice assistant already existed but was limited to search only — it couldn't help with registration, subscription, or shopping, where users needed it most.
en.case.faintv.situation.challenge3: Checkout flows required entering personal details, addresses, and invoice information via D-pad, leading to high drop-off among elderly users.
en.case.faintv.owned.label: What I owned
en.case.faintv.owned.item1: TV information architecture and interaction design
en.case.faintv.owned.item2: Voice search and T-commerce experience on TV
en.case.faintv.owned.item3: Cross-device task allocation and TV ↔ Mobile handoff design
en.case.faintv.owned.item4: User research and interviews (50+ participants)
en.case.faintv.outcome.label: Outcome
en.case.faintv.outcome.body: In usability testing, redesigning FainTV's login flow increased task completion among elderly users from 30% to 80% — validating a voice-first, lower-input direction on TV.
en.case.faintv.task.label: T — Task
en.case.faintv.task.title: Elderly users could discover content — but couldn't complete what came next.
en.case.faintv.task.problem1: Typing on TV is painful — many give up or ask family before completing a search.
en.case.faintv.task.problem2: Payment and invoice details via remote are so slow and error-prone most rely on family to finish.
en.case.faintv.task.problem3: Voice can find content, but doesn't help with registration, subscription, or checkout.
en.case.faintv.task.goal1: Complete core tasks in as few clear steps as possible — minimal remote input.
en.case.faintv.task.goal2: Clarify which steps belong on TV and which should move to mobile or web.
en.case.faintv.task.goal3: Keep the experience simple enough for elderly users to operate independently.
en.case.faintv.task.challenge.label: Design challenge
en.case.faintv.task.challenge.body: Redesign FainTV so that TV does what it's best at — browsing, voice search, and confirming decisions — and mobile handles the rest.
en.case.faintv.task.punchline: The problem isn't the form — it's that the form is on the wrong device.
en.case.faintv.action.label: A — Action
en.case.faintv.action.title: Four phases — from discovering the pain, to proving the cross-device solution worked.
en.case.faintv.action.discover.name: Discover
en.case.faintv.action.discover.desc: Interviews with 50+ users confirmed that registration, payment, and invoice steps caused the most drop-off on TV.
en.case.faintv.action.define.name: Define
en.case.faintv.action.define.desc: Split tasks into TV-native vs. not. Core hypothesis: TV for deciding, mobile for filling and paying.
en.case.faintv.action.design.name: Design
en.case.faintv.action.design.desc: Designed TV voice search and T-commerce. Proposed "start on TV, finish on mobile" for subscription and checkout.
en.case.faintv.action.test.name: Test & learn
en.case.faintv.action.test.desc: Voice search was well-received but long form-based steps still caused friction — validating the cross-device solution.
en.case.faintv.action.insight.label: Key insight from testing
en.case.faintv.action.insight.body: Users loved using voice for content discovery, but still got stuck whenever the TV asked them to type. This confirmed that input friction was a device problem, not a user problem.
en.case.faintv.strategy.label: A — Strategy
en.case.faintv.strategy.title: Not every task belongs on every screen.
en.case.faintv.strategy.body: Designing for elderly users means choosing the right device for each moment — based on input effort, context, and who might be helping — not cramming everything into one interface.
en.case.faintv.strategy.tv.name: TV
en.case.faintv.strategy.tv.headline: Low-input, high-immersion
en.case.faintv.strategy.tv.desc: Browse, watch, and confirm — no typing required
en.case.faintv.strategy.mobile.name: Mobile
en.case.faintv.strategy.mobile.headline: High-input, personal, on-hand
en.case.faintv.strategy.mobile.desc: Type, pay, verify — familiar touchscreen input
en.case.faintv.strategy.web.name: Web
en.case.faintv.strategy.web.headline: Management & long-term records
en.case.faintv.strategy.table.intro: What belongs on TV — what moves to mobile — what shifts to web
en.case.faintv.strategy.why.tv.title: Why "confirm purchase" stays on TV
en.case.faintv.strategy.why.tv.body: The decision moment belongs on the engaged screen. Moving intent to mobile mid-viewing breaks flow for elderly users.
en.case.faintv.strategy.why.mobile.title: Why login & payment leave the TV
en.case.faintv.strategy.why.mobile.body: SMS codes, passwords, card numbers — all fight against a 10-foot, D-pad-only environment. Highest drop-off in testing.
en.case.faintv.strategy.why.web.title: Why caregiver tasks live on web
en.case.faintv.strategy.why.web.body: Family members need full-screen management tools, not an elderly-optimised TV interface. Separating concerns keeps both clean.
en.case.faintv.strategy.punchline: "I don't design screens — I design which screen each task belongs on."
en.case.faintv.voice.label: A — Voice design
en.case.faintv.voice.title: Voice as the primary input — not just a search shortcut.
en.case.faintv.voice.constraints.label: 10-foot constraints
en.case.faintv.voice.constraints.body: Safe-area padding, large type (min 36px) and high-contrast focus rings. All content navigable with a D-pad only.
en.case.faintv.voice.why.label: Why voice, not keyboard
en.case.faintv.voice.why.body: 65% of elderly users struggled with the on-screen keyboard. Voice reduces a 20-step search into just 2 steps.
en.case.faintv.voice.step1.title: Press and hold the voice button
en.case.faintv.voice.step1.desc: A single button on the remote — no menu navigation needed
en.case.faintv.voice.step2.title: Say a title, actor, or genre
en.case.faintv.voice.step2.desc: "Show me dramas with Chen Bo-lin" or simply "news"
en.case.faintv.voice.step3.title: Jump directly to content
en.case.faintv.voice.step3.desc: No intermediate screens — users land on results immediately
en.case.faintv.voice.insight.label: Why this matters
en.case.faintv.voice.insight.body: Voice wasn't just a convenience feature — it was the bridge between the TV and the rest of the cross-device system. Without it, elderly users had no reliable way to initiate a task on TV.
en.case.faintv.pain.label: A — The pain point
en.case.faintv.pain.title: The form isn't the problem. The device is.
en.case.faintv.pain.body: Elderly users could discover products on TV — but many abandoned the flow as soon as checkout began. The remote turned a 2-minute task into a 12–15 minute ordeal.
en.case.faintv.pain.stat1.title: Average time: 12–15 minutes
en.case.faintv.pain.stat1.body: Most users under 60 took under 3 minutes on mobile for the same flow.
en.case.faintv.pain.stat2.title: Most abandoned at credit card field
en.case.faintv.pain.stat2.body: 16 digits via D-pad — the single biggest drop-off point across all sessions.
en.case.faintv.pain.stat3.title: "I just asked my daughter to do it"
en.case.faintv.pain.stat3.body: A recurring quote. Task completion depended on family availability.
en.case.faintv.pain.reframe.label: The reframe
en.case.faintv.pain.reframe.body: These aren't bad forms. They're forms on the wrong device. The solution isn't to simplify the form — it's to move it to mobile.
en.case.faintv.handoff.label: A — Handoff flow
en.case.faintv.handoff.title: Start on TV. Finish on mobile.
en.case.faintv.handoff.body: TV stays in control of the viewing and decision moment. Mobile takes over the moment high-effort input is required. The handoff is one tap — or one QR scan.
en.case.faintv.handoff.step1.title: Product appears during broadcast
en.case.faintv.handoff.step1.desc: Lightweight CTA overlay: "Press red to buy"
en.case.faintv.handoff.step2.title: User confirms intent
en.case.faintv.handoff.mid.label: Handoff
en.case.faintv.handoff.mid.title: QR code on TV or push notification to phone
en.case.faintv.handoff.mid.desc: One scan or one tap — the critical device transition
en.case.faintv.handoff.step3.title: Mobile opens checkout
en.case.faintv.handoff.step3.desc: Member data pre-filled — address and payment only
en.case.faintv.handoff.step4.title: Complete payment on mobile
en.case.faintv.handoff.step5.title: TV confirms success
en.case.faintv.handoff.step5.desc: Brief confirmation, then auto-returns to content
en.case.faintv.handoff.insight.label: Why this works
en.case.faintv.handoff.insight.body: Mobile checkout keeps the momentum going after the handoff. TV keeps the decision moment. Mobile handles all input.
en.case.faintv.screens.label: A — Key screens
en.case.faintv.screens.title: Four moments that tell the full story.
en.case.faintv.screens.cta.title: TV · Product CTA overlay
en.case.faintv.screens.cta.desc: Non-intrusive product prompt during broadcast. One button triggers the handoff.
en.case.faintv.screens.handoff.title: TV · Handoff moment
en.case.faintv.screens.handoff.desc: QR code on screen + push notification sent. The critical device transition.
en.case.faintv.screens.checkout.title: Mobile · Checkout
en.case.faintv.screens.checkout.desc: Pre-filled member data, touchscreen input. Typically around 2 minutes.
en.case.faintv.screens.confirmed.title: TV · Purchase confirmed
en.case.faintv.screens.confirmed.desc: Brief confirmation, then auto-returns to viewing. Loop closed on TV.
en.case.faintv.result.body: By moving high-input tasks off the TV and validating a cross-device handoff strategy, the redesign confirmed that device-fit matters more than interface polish.
en.case.faintv.impact.summary: Task completion among elderly users increased by 50 percentage points — validating a voice-first, lower-input direction on TV.
en.case.faintv.impact.stat65: Initially struggled with text-based search — voice search significantly reduced this friction.
en.case.faintv.impact.stat2min: Average checkout on mobile, vs 12–15 minutes via TV D-pad input.
en.case.faintv.impact.stat50: Participants across user research and usability testing sessions.
en.case.faintv.learned.label: What I learned
en.case.faintv.learned.body: Designing for elderly users isn't just about making things bigger — it's about eliminating interactions that require long, sustained input. Voice should be a connector across devices, not just a search shortcut inside a single interface.
en.case.faintv.nextsteps.label: Next steps
en.case.faintv.nextsteps.body: Design the caregiver experience on web, explore an emergency SOS button integrated into the voice and cross-device system — and test the QR-based handoff with non-smartphone-native elderly users.

zh.case.genebook.overview.label: 概述
zh.case.genebook.overview.body: 適逢台灣生物科技領導品牌康健科技成立十週年，我主導為期四個月的全面品牌再造。作為主導產品設計師，我負責企業識別（CI）與官方網站的端到端轉型——將品牌從傳統「B2B 實驗室」形象，調整為專業且具溫度的「以人為本的健康夥伴」。
zh.case.genebook.problem.label: 問題
zh.case.genebook.problem.headline: 一個十年品牌停留在「B2B 實驗室」定位，難以觸及當代健康意識消費者。
zh.case.genebook.problem.challenge.label: 品牌挑戰
zh.case.genebook.problem.challenge.body: 康健科技既有識別偏冷、偏臨床，對實驗室夥伴有效，卻讓一般大眾卻步。品牌需要同時傳達信任、現代感與親和力——且不能失去科學可信度。此外，專業醫療術語（例如「NGS」）對一般使用者既陌生也難以理解。
zh.case.genebook.insight.label: 關鍵策略洞察
zh.case.genebook.insight.body: 在外部測試中，我發現將「高科技」轉譯為「高價值」——凸顯設備的市場價值與高階定價——即使沒有醫療背景的使用者，也能立刻建立信任。
zh.case.genebook.process.label: 流程
zh.case.genebook.process.headline: 探索 → 架構 → 驗證 → 策略精煉。
zh.case.genebook.process.01.name: 探索
zh.case.genebook.process.01.desc: 透過利害關係人訪談釐清品牌再造的「Why」。競爭分析找出市場缺口與差異化機會。
zh.case.genebook.process.02.name: 架構
zh.case.genebook.process.02.desc: 建立清晰的資訊架構，簡化複雜的基因檢測服務。內部可用性測試優化導覽列，並簡化「操作步驟」。
zh.case.genebook.process.03.name: 高保真設計
zh.case.genebook.process.03.desc: 將新 CI 整合進高保真網頁介面。與潛在使用者進行外部可用性測試，驗證介面並浮現關鍵信任洞察。
zh.case.genebook.process.04.name: 策略精煉
zh.case.genebook.process.04.desc: 跳脫技術術語，改為策略性凸顯市場價值——把複雜科學轉譯為可感知的品質，立即建立使用者信任。
zh.case.genebook.solution.label: 解法
zh.case.genebook.solution.headline: 以摩斯密碼作為 DNA 隱喻——將品牌重新定位為「生物科技解密者」。
zh.case.genebook.solution.identity.label: 品牌識別
zh.case.genebook.solution.identity.body: 我以摩斯密碼（Morse Code）為靈感，取代過時的人形商標——象徵 DNA 是生命的「原始碼」，康健科技則是專業的「解碼者」。我捨棄生技常見的藍與綠，改以活力橙與專業紅作為主色，為品牌注入活力與親和力。
zh.case.genebook.solution.system.label: 系統化
zh.case.genebook.solution.system.body: 為確保長期可擴展性，我交付完整的CI 品牌手冊，涵蓋標誌規範、12 欄格系統與統一設計元件——讓系統從第一天就能完成設計交付。
zh.case.genebook.impact.label: 的使用者重視內容品質勝過價格
zh.case.genebook.impact.desc: 質性研究確認，以清晰圖表呈現檢測流程是最有效的信任建立機制——並據此決定最終資訊層級。
zh.case.genebook.outcome.label: 成果
zh.case.genebook.outcome.headline: 全面的品牌轉型——科學嚴謹與人文溫度並存。
zh.case.genebook.outcome.strategic.title: 策略設計與品牌
zh.case.genebook.outcome.strategic.1: 全面轉型：整合平面設計、UI 設計與 CI，完成這家台灣指標性生物科技公司的品牌重塑。
zh.case.genebook.outcome.strategic.2: 敘事識別：以 Morse Code 將品牌重新定位為「生物科技解密者」。
zh.case.genebook.outcome.strategic.3: 情感連結：從冷調臨床色系，轉為具活力與年輕感的色彩。
zh.case.genebook.outcome.strategic.4: 系統可擴展性：交付嚴謹的 CI 手冊，含標誌、12 欄格與字型規範。
zh.case.genebook.outcome.ux.title: 以使用者為中心的 UX 洞察
zh.case.genebook.outcome.ux.1: 以透明建立信任：凸顯設備市場價值，補上一般大眾的知識落差。
zh.case.genebook.outcome.ux.2: 直覺資訊架構：優化導覽列並簡化操作步驟，降低複雜基因資訊的理解門檻。
zh.case.genebook.outcome.ux.3: 可執行數據：80% 的使用者重視高品質內容勝過價格——再次確認清晰流程圖的必要性。

zh.case.tfl.overview.label: 概述
zh.case.tfl.overview.body: 健身 App 市場雖已飽和，流失率仍高。多數產品失敗在於：使用者在高強度訓練中還得應付複雜資料輸入。我的目標是設計一套低摩擦的追蹤系統，維持訓練節奏並提升長期參與——把獨處的鍛鍊，轉成有溫度、以人為本的體驗。
zh.case.tfl.strategy.label: 策略
zh.case.tfl.strategy.headline: Triple W 框架——Why、How、What——確保每個決策都立足於使用者。
zh.case.tfl.strategy.01.name: 盤點
zh.case.tfl.strategy.01.desc: 進行競爭分析，找出一線健身 App 的導覽瓶頸。既有產品缺少教練追蹤與社群功能。
zh.case.tfl.strategy.02.name: 設計
zh.case.tfl.strategy.02.desc: 導入手勢導覽與預測式資料輸入，降低訓練中的認知負荷。資訊架構與 Task Flow 作為 Deliver 階段的藍圖。
zh.case.tfl.strategy.03.name: 驗證
zh.case.tfl.strategy.03.desc: 與五位現役重訓者進行可用性測試，衡量任務完成速度與流程滿意度。Design Review 階段整合訪談回饋與工程可行性。
zh.case.tfl.design.label: 設計
zh.case.tfl.design.headline: 連結專業指導與社交連結——不只是追蹤數字。
zh.case.tfl.design.scalability.label: 可擴展性
zh.case.tfl.design.scalability.body: 建立完整設計系統，確保視覺一致性，並讓工程設計交付加快兩倍。在最終交付前，Design Review 階段整合使用者訪談回饋與技術可行性評估。
zh.case.tfl.conclusion.label: 結語
zh.case.tfl.conclusion.body: 「超越追蹤：以連結與洞察提升健身旅程。」

zh.case.vcue.hero.title: Visual Cues Study
zh.case.vcue.hero.subtitle: 健身教學影片中的視覺線索如何影響初學者的動作學習——一項三階段混合研究法，產出一套原創的設計框架。
zh.case.vcue.meta.role.label: 角色
zh.case.vcue.meta.institution.label: 機構
zh.case.vcue.meta.duration.label: 專案時長
zh.case.vcue.meta.methods.label: 研究方法
zh.case.vcue.meta.methods.value: 問卷調查・可用性測試・專家評估
zh.case.vcue.overview.label: 概述
zh.case.vcue.overview.body: 這項研究探討健身教學影片中的視覺線索如何影響初學者的動作學習。透過三階段研究法，我評估了四種視覺線索——方向型、量測型、身體標示型、隱喻型——並同時分析量化的表現數據與質化的使用者洞察。研究最終產出一套原創的設計框架：認知負荷與學習成效動態平衡模型。
zh.case.vcue.gap.label: 研究缺口
zh.case.vcue.gap.headline: 86% 的人靠影片學習身體技能。但幾乎沒有人研究過，這些影片到底有沒有用。
zh.case.vcue.gap.problem.label: 問題所在
zh.case.vcue.gap.problem.body: 數位學習從根本上改變了初學者接觸體能訓練的方式。超過 70% 的使用者靠 YouTube 學深蹲、伸展這類動作。但在沒有專業指導的情況下，學習者經常模仿錯誤，導致姿勢不良、增加受傷風險。更深層的問題是系統性的：現有教學影片的視覺線索設計，靠的是直覺與美感偏好，不是證據。目前沒有任何一套公認有效的設計準則。
zh.case.vcue.gap.context.label: 研究脈絡
zh.case.vcue.gap.context.body: 過去的研究多聚焦在 VR／AR 與互動系統，以影片為主的動作學習長期被系統性地忽略。這項研究從認知負荷理論與外部注意力理論出發，補上這塊研究缺口，檢視四種線索類型。
zh.case.vcue.question.label: 研究問題
zh.case.vcue.question.body: 四種視覺線索——方向型、量測型、身體標示型、隱喻型——如何在教學影片中支持並提升初學者的動作學習？
zh.case.vcue.methodology.label: 研究方法
zh.case.vcue.methodology.headline: 三階段混合研究法——量化與質化並行，初學者與專家並重。
zh.case.vcue.methodology.survey.name: 線上問卷
zh.case.vcue.methodology.survey.body: 透過社群媒體與大學網絡，發送給 18 到 40 歲的健身初學者。問卷調查了六種視覺線索的學習習慣、觀影行為與初步偏好，包括骨架疊圖與肌肉啟動標示。根據參與者的回饋，篩選出四種線索類型作為後續測試的重點。
zh.case.vcue.methodology.usability.name: 可用性測試
zh.case.vcue.methodology.usability.body: 每位參與者觀看四支簡短的深蹲教學影片，各自嵌入不同的視覺線索類型，並全程觀察記錄其表現。任務結束後的訪談蒐集了關於清晰度、幫助程度與主觀認知負荷的質化洞察，並用平衡對抗設計控制順序效應。
zh.case.vcue.methodology.expert.name: 專家評估
zh.case.vcue.methodology.expert.tag: 10 位教練與從業者・三角驗證
zh.case.vcue.methodology.expert.body: 教練、私人教練與資深運動者評估一支整合了全部四種線索類型的優化影片。這個階段蒐集了專業驗證與批判性觀點，讓新手與專家的反應得以交叉比對——結果發現不同經驗程度的人，對線索的感受有明顯落差。
zh.case.vcue.premise.label: 核心命題
zh.case.vcue.premise.body: 多數教學影片的設計都建立在直覺與美感偏好上，而非證據。這項研究針對初學者的動作學習，系統性地為四種線索類型排序——讓設計決策建立在觀察到的數據上，而不是假設。
zh.case.vcue.experiment.label: 實驗設計
zh.case.vcue.experiment.headline: 四種線索類型，同一個深蹲動作，在相同條件下，對同一群初學者進行測量。
zh.case.vcue.experiment.directional.name: 方向型線索
zh.case.vcue.experiment.directional.def: 用箭頭與動線標示動作的方向與路徑，立即傳達身體該往哪裡移動，減少施力方向與軌跡的模糊地帶。
zh.case.vcue.experiment.directional.verdict: 最佳區間——最適合初學者
zh.case.vcue.experiment.highlight.name: 身體標示型線索
zh.case.vcue.experiment.highlight.def: 在動作過程中用發光或色彩強調特定肌群或關節，把注意力引導到該啟動的部位，支持身體感知與本體感覺。
zh.case.vcue.experiment.highlight.verdict: 有幫助——但出現頻率需要控制
zh.case.vcue.experiment.metaphor.name: 隱喻型線索
zh.case.vcue.experiment.metaphor.def: 用生活化的比喻，把抽象的動作概念轉譯成熟悉的畫面——例如「像坐進一張看不見的椅子」。需要仰賴過去的經驗才能正確解讀。
zh.case.vcue.experiment.measurement.name: 量測型線索
zh.case.vcue.experiment.measurement.def: 在身體上疊加角度線、度數標記與深度指標。提供精確的數字參考，但需要抽象判讀，對初學者來說負荷過重。
zh.case.vcue.experiment.measurement.verdict: 混淆區間——精確但負荷過高
zh.case.vcue.qual.label: 質化研究發現
zh.case.vcue.qual.headline: Gioia 編碼法讓線索之間的層級關係清楚浮現：每種線索扮演不同角色——對初學者來說，代價也不一樣。
zh.case.vcue.qual.directional.name: 方向型
zh.case.vcue.qual.directional.body: 提供即時的動作指引與修正回饋。參與者普遍認為一目瞭然，認知成本也最低——但對比不足、缺乏動態或時機不對時，箭頭可能會被當成介面裝飾，而不是教學指引。
zh.case.vcue.qual.highlight.name: 身體標示型
zh.case.vcue.qual.highlight.body: 把注意力引導到肌肉啟動與姿勢控制上。時機抓得好就很有幫助；但出現節奏與是否過度使用，是質化訪談中浮現的主要風險。
zh.case.vcue.qual.metaphor.name: 隱喻型
zh.case.vcue.qual.metaphor.body: 透過比喻傳達動作。對有運動經驗的參與者來說很直覺——但對真正的初學者而言，既模糊又難以體會。
zh.case.vcue.qual.measurement.name: 量測型
zh.case.vcue.qual.measurement.body: 提供精確度與標準，但抽象的數字很難轉譯成身體動作。認知負荷高，對初學者的實際幫助卻有限。
zh.case.vcue.qual.cross.label: 跨線索觀察
zh.case.vcue.qual.cross.item1: 各線索之間的差異在於功能，不只是喜好排名：指引、聚焦注意力、類比、精確度，各司其職。
zh.case.vcue.qual.cross.item2: 精確度高≠適合初學者：量測型在質化訪談中的反應，正好解釋了它在量化數據上表現不佳的原因。
zh.case.vcue.qual.cross.item3: 從編碼分析得出的設計優先順序：先求視覺清晰，再談出現時機與節奏；避免同時疊加太多種線索類型。
zh.case.vcue.qual.bridge.label: 從編碼到模型
zh.case.vcue.qual.bridge.body: 比較四棵編碼樹之間的角色差異——而不只是研究者的直覺——是動態平衡模型（學習成效 × 認知負荷）的立論基礎。下一段的量化分數，也與這些質化角色互相呼應。
zh.case.vcue.qual.method.label: 研究方法
zh.case.vcue.qual.method.body: 對初學者可用性測試後的訪談逐字稿，採用歸納式 Gioia 編碼法（第一階概念 → 第二階主題 → 聚合維度）進行分析。分析依線索類型分別進行，產出四棵可互相比較的編碼樹。在進入理論化之前先貼近參與者的原始語言，確保這套框架反映的是使用者真正說的話，而不是研究者的假設。
zh.case.vcue.qual.derived: 結論是如何推導出來的

zh.case.vcue.qual.order1.desc: 將參與者的原始語句標記為浮現的描述性代碼——用詞盡量貼近受訪者本人的話
zh.case.vcue.qual.order2.title: 第二階主題
zh.case.vcue.qual.order2.desc: 將第一階代碼依概念相似性歸類為研究者辨識出的理論類別
zh.case.vcue.qual.order3.title: 聚合維度
zh.case.vcue.qual.order3.desc: 將第二階主題整合為能解釋潛在現象的高層次理論建構

zh.case.vcue.gioia.meas.insight: 數字上很精確——但難以體會，負荷高
zh.case.vcue.findings.label: 研究發現
zh.case.vcue.findings.headline: 明確的層級關係浮現出來——不是每種視覺線索，都能同樣幫助初學者。
zh.case.vcue.findings.source.label: 資料來源
zh.case.vcue.findings.source.body: 以下分數與上方的質化角色互相呼應。分數為受測後自陳問卷的李克特量表平均值（n=10 位初學者，第一輪可用性測試）。每位參與者以平衡對抗順序觀看全部四支線索影片，並在看完後立即評分。成效取自論文表 2 中的偏好維度；認知負荷取自自陳的心智努力維度。完整的六維度數據（有用性、清晰度、分心程度、心智努力、投入度、偏好度）與標準差，詳見論文表 2。

zh.case.vcue.vs.label: 初學者 vs 專家
zh.case.vcue.vs.headline: 經驗改變了一切。同一種線索，看在不同人眼裡，效果完全不同。
zh.case.vcue.vs.divergence.label: 關鍵落差
zh.case.vcue.vs.divergence.body: 專家評估者給隱喻型線索的評分明顯高於初學者——因為他們已經具備解讀抽象比喻所需的概念框架。對初學者來說，同一種線索反而造成困惑。量測型線索則呈現相反的模式：專家重視精確度，但初學者被數字淹沒，無法把它們對應到實際的身體動作。這個落差證實了視覺線索的設計無法一體適用。

zh.case.vcue.vs.dir.name: 方向型
zh.case.vcue.vs.dir.note: 各組意見一致——公認最清楚的線索

zh.case.vcue.vs.hl.note: 專家給的回饋更精確——點出了時機與過度使用的風險
zh.case.vcue.vs.met.name: 隱喻型
zh.case.vcue.vs.met.note: 專家覺得直覺又好記；初學者若缺乏脈絡則覺得模糊

zh.case.vcue.model.label: 原創框架
zh.case.vcue.model.headline: 動態平衡模型——把視覺線索放進「學習成效」與「認知成本」的張力關係中定位。
zh.case.vcue.model.theModel.label: 這套模型
zh.case.vcue.model.theModel.body: 這項研究最主要的貢獻，是一套用來評估教學用視覺線索的雙軸框架。透過把學習成效與認知負荷兩軸交叉對照，這套模型劃分出四個區間——最佳、過載、無效、混淆——為影片設計者提供可直接應用的指引。這套模型也點出了雙面刃效應：同時整合多種線索會提升專業感與可信度，但也會提高認知負荷，可能反而削弱學習效率。
zh.case.vcue.model.overload.desc:
高成效，但
對學習者代價高
zh.case.vcue.sword.label: 關鍵發現
zh.case.vcue.sword.body: 雙面刃效應：同時整合多種視覺線索會提升專業感與信任度——但也會提高認知負荷、可能分散注意力，最終降低整體學習效率。
zh.case.vcue.principles.label: 設計原則
zh.case.vcue.principles.headline: 給教學影片創作者的八條實證設計準則。
zh.case.vcue.principles.selection.title: 線索選擇
zh.case.vcue.principles.selection.item1: 優先使用方向型線索，提供清楚、即時的動作指引。
zh.case.vcue.principles.selection.item2: 用身體標示型線索聚焦關鍵部位——但避免過度使用。
zh.case.vcue.principles.selection.item3: 謹慎使用量測型線索，數字可能讓初學者感到困惑。
zh.case.vcue.principles.selection.item4: 依情境使用隱喻型線索——對有經驗的學習者效果較好。
zh.case.vcue.principles.delivery.title: 呈現與結構
zh.case.vcue.principles.delivery.item1: 確保線索在關鍵動作時機準時出現。
zh.case.vcue.principles.delivery.item2: 影片長度控制在短時間內（約 90 秒），符合初學者的注意力與偏好。
zh.case.vcue.principles.delivery.item3: 同時出現的線索類型不要超過兩種——避免認知過載。
zh.case.vcue.principles.delivery.item4: 搭配多個拍攝角度，減少視覺死角，照顧不同學習者的需求。
zh.case.vcue.reflection.label: 反思
zh.case.vcue.reflection.headline: 用證據設計、而不是靠假設，究竟意味著什麼。
zh.case.vcue.reflection.researcher.label: 作為研究者
zh.case.vcue.reflection.researcher.body: 這個專案讓我更加確信，設計決策必須建立在證據之上。從問卷到可用性測試再到專家評估的多階段研究法，讓我看見單一方法會漏掉多少東西，也讓我理解三角驗證如何建立可信度。Gioia 編碼的過程，把參與者的原始語句轉化成一套結構化的框架，揭露了單憑直覺看不出來的模式。
zh.case.vcue.reflection.designer.label: 作為設計師
zh.case.vcue.reflection.designer.body: 最讓我意外的發現是經驗落差：專家覺得直覺的線索，對初學者來說反而造成困惑。這也讓我把一個原則帶進日後每個設計專案：你自己對一套系統有多熟悉，恰恰是判斷它易用性最不可靠的指標。要為「還不知道你所知道的事」的人設計，需要刻意的研究，光靠同理心是不夠的。
zh.case.vcue.reflection.limitations.label: 研究限制
zh.case.vcue.reflection.limitations.body: 這項研究有幾個值得說明的限制。樣本數不大——可用性測試 10 位初學者、專家評估 10 位——統計上的可推論性有限。研究結果建立在單一動作（深蹲）上，未必能直接套用到其他運動或動作技能領域。認知負荷是透過自陳量表測量，而非生理指標，可能帶有主觀偏誤。此外，受控的研究環境也和真實世界的影片觀看情境不完全相同。這些限制在早期探索性研究中很常見，也點出了未來研究可以延伸的方向。
zh.case.vcue.experiment.metaphor.verdict: 較適合有經驗者——新手較難理解

zh.case.overheadflights.situation.title: 主流應用都要求你主動開啟、主動搜尋；被動、單機的方向，硬體已經做過了。
zh.case.overheadflights.situation.market.p1: 多數人一天裡大部分時間都黏在手機或筆電上。這個產品從這個觀察出發：把螢幕保護程式接上真實航班資訊，用盡可能低的干擾，讓人隱約感覺到與另一個人的連結。
zh.case.overheadflights.situation.market.p2: 追蹤飛機的工具並不缺——FlightRadar24、Plane Finder、FlightAware 都把整片天空攤成地圖、列表、警示動態。它們要求你主動開啟應用才能查看；本質上是儀表板。Maker 社群也做過硬體：Airframe（Raspberry Pi + 電子紙）安靜地顯示頭頂最近的那架飛機——是作者為住在航道下方的朋友做的禮物。這個想法本身，並不是我先想到的。
zh.case.overheadflights.situation.row2.limi: 需要買零件、組裝，佔實體空間
zh.case.overheadflights.situation.row3.limi: 沒有航班資訊，或與航班無關
zh.case.overheadflights.positioning.label: 定位
zh.case.overheadflights.positioning.title: 缺口不在「頭頂有飛機」這個想法——而在交叉點：macOS 螢幕保護程式。
zh.case.overheadflights.positioning.body: 核對之後，真正的缺口不是「頭頂有飛機」這個概念，而是交叉點：macOS 螢幕保護程式 × 真實航班資料 × 編輯式排版。主流應用的商業模式不鼓勵被動的螢幕保護程式；Airframe 證明被動、單機的方向可行，但它多了一個實體裝置。用軟體螢幕保護程式做這件事，沒有直接先例——論證必須正面面對 Airframe，而不是假裝市場是空的。
zh.case.overheadflights.integrity.label: 資料真實性
zh.case.overheadflights.integrity.body: 作品集 mockup 可以看起來很美，但如果主張是「頭頂有飛機」，資料必須是即時 ADS-B——不是假的呼號動畫。資料來源的使用條款（非商業／教育／個人）也必須先核過，才能寫進 README。
zh.case.overheadflights.task.label: 任務
zh.case.overheadflights.task.title: 把原本只存在追蹤應用裡的即時資料，搬進電腦本來就在跑的螢幕保護程式。
zh.case.overheadflights.task.goal.label: 目標
zh.case.overheadflights.task.goal.body: 把即時資料——此刻飛過頭頂的那架飛機，原本只活在追蹤應用裡的資訊——搬進電腦本來就在跑的螢幕保護程式。不新增應用、不新增裝置、不主動搜尋：只替換螢幕保護程式顯示的內容，讓人幾乎不被打擾的同時，隱約感覺到一點人與人的連結。
zh.case.overheadflights.task.quote: 「我決定做一個安靜顯示航班資訊的螢幕保護程式，讓人不必費力就能感到連結。」
zh.case.overheadflights.task.role: 角色：獨立構思並決定方向、視覺、取捨與風險。AI 協作研究整理、起草與實作——規則如下。
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.label: 行動 · AI
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.title: 四個工具，各有職分——每一步我都是把關者。
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.collab.label: 協作
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.collab.intro: 這不是把一個 prompt 丟給工具然後等結果。四個工具，各有明確職分，每一步我都是把關者：
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.claude.role: 第一輪思考：拆解問題、整理市場研究、起草規格、早期技術取捨
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.perplexity.role: 核對主張：找原始文件與研究，檢查市場研究與設計論證裡的說法是否站得住
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.grok.role: 只抓錯：不重做思考；檢視事實、假設、風險
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.cursor.role: 只執行已通過審核的任務包；審核前不自行發揮
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.perplexity.why: 選 Perplexity 的理由很直接：通用 AI 的回答偶爾聽起來很有權威，背後卻沒有真實來源。Perplexity 會附上來源，讓我可以回頭核對，而不是照單全收。這對一份會被仔細檢視的作品集論證很重要——市場研究裡「缺口在哪」的主張，以及設計論證引用的研究，都必須能追溯到真實文件，而不是「AI 說的」。
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.gatekeeping.titl: 把關實例（這不是流程展示——這就是判斷本身）
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.gate.1: Perplexity 的 MCP 工具一直回 404。我沒有等工具修好，也沒有用 AI 未經核對的記憶來填洞——我自己開瀏覽器，手動核對研究。判斷是：工具失敗時，有「先寫下來、之後再核」和「直接手動做」兩條路。我選後者，因為這份市場研究最終要支撐「這個缺口是真的」——經不起建立在未核對的資訊上。
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.gate.2: 草稿想把 adsbdb 的速率限制寫成一個具體數字。那個數字從未對過原始來源——只是 AI 聽起來合理的猜測。我要求「沒有原始來源核對，就不寫數字」，改成保守、可核對的措辭（例如「遠低於公開的 1 req/s 上限」——可查，但不誇大）。判斷是：作品集會被檢視，沒有來源的數字，比沒有數字更傷可信度。
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.gate.3: AI 翻出一個對我不利的先例：Airframe。比較安全的做法是避而不談，讓讀者以為這個想法是原創。我選擇正面面對：承認 Airframe 更早做過「頭頂最近的飛機」這個概念，把差異收斂到「形式（螢幕保護程式 vs. 硬體）+ 執行（編輯式排版 vs. 電子紙）」。判斷是：沒找到競爭者，不代表你贏了。願意正面面對你找到的競爭者，才真正展現產品判斷——而不是市場研究有多完整。
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.gate.4: 視覺設計定稿後，我在文件裡把它標成凍結。我明確告訴 AI：「文字大小與版面已經對了——除非我說，否則不要動」——把它剩下的自由度限制在資料層與背景效果。判斷是：AI 沒有內建的「夠好了、停在這裡」——放著不管，它會持續微調到看不出差別之後還在調。凍結設計是我刻意畫的線；不是 AI 自己收斂出來的。
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.principle.label: 原則
zh.case.overheadflights.ai.principle.body: AI 加速草稿與實作。過不過關，是我的決定。
zh.case.overheadflights.research.label: 行動 · 研究與設計
zh.case.overheadflights.research.title: 先核對市場缺口是否真實，再決定哪些框架真正支撐「安靜」。
zh.case.overheadflights.research.step1: 先定義問題本身，再急著找研究工具。真正的缺口是「追蹤飛機」這個功能，還是「不必主動查看、也能被動注意到」這種體驗？問題定義錯了，後面再多的競品研究也補不回來。
zh.case.overheadflights.research.step2: 掃描主流應用的產品邏輯與交付形式（FlightRadar24、Plane Finder、FlightAware），確認它們的核心假設是「使用者會主動開啟應用來查看」。這個假設本身才是市場結構裡真正的限制——不只是隨手選的描述詞。
zh.case.overheadflights.research.step3: 再往下查 maker 專案、文章與 GitHub（Airframe、FlightTracker 等），刻意找對自己主張不利的先例，避免說服自己市場是空的。這一步存在，是為了讓情境區塊的定位陳述能撐過最直接的反駁：「不是已經有人做過了嗎？」
zh.case.overheadflights.research.step4: 用原始文件核對 API 條款（airplanes.live 的速率限制、使用條款）。沒有原始來源的數字不進對外文件——寧可使用保守、可核對的措辭，也不要用看起來更精確、卻無從追溯的數字。
zh.case.overheadflights.research.step5: 收斂成一句經得起挑戰的定位陳述：承認先例存在，把真正的差異壓成兩點——「螢幕保護程式作為媒介」+「編輯式排版作為執行」——而不是含糊地說「沒有類似的東西」。
zh.case.overheadflights.research.design.int: 三個框架，各一行，然後落到實際數字：
zh.case.overheadflights.research.framework1: Calm technology（Weiser & Brown, 1995）：資訊留在注意力的周邊，只在需要時移到中心。原文的動機是對抗資訊過載造成的焦慮——不只是節省注意力。
zh.case.overheadflights.research.framework2: Soft fascination（注意力恢復，Kaplan & Kaplan, 1989）：不費力、溫和的刺激（像看雲）讓注意力在長時間專注後得以休息。這就是這個產品活在「閒置／鎖定畫面」時刻的理由——它要服務的是休息的片刻，而不是再加一個需要處理的資訊來源。
zh.case.overheadflights.research.framework3: Ambient intimacy / social snacking（Reichelt, 2007; Gardner, Pickett & Knowles, 2005）：被動接觸另一個人存在的象徵——即使沒有任何互動——也能降低孤立感。陌生人的航班安靜出現，是一個小小的訊號：「外面有人正在過自己的生活」，幾乎像有人靜靜地來確認你還在。
zh.case.overheadflights.research.visual.tit: 這三個框架如何變成實際的視覺決定：
zh.case.overheadflights.research.visual.1: 喚起程度由亮度與飽和度驅動，不是色相（Valdez & Mehrabian, 1994）——這是近黑背景（rgb(0.02, 0.02, 0.025)）加上低飽和銀白文字的依據。不必靠「冷色」這種陳腔來製造平靜——直接把亮度與飽和度降下來就夠了。
zh.case.overheadflights.research.visual.2: 文字層級用比例透明度遞減，不是等距階梯：呼號 0.82 → 航空公司 0.48 → meta 0.34 → 字母標記 0.28。這種比例遞減對應眼睛對亮度差的非線性知覺（Weber-Fechner）——在低對比環境裡，比例階梯讓每一層層級感覺均勻，而不是用強烈對比硬擠層級。
zh.case.overheadflights.research.visual.3: 沒有卡片、沒有邊框、沒有圖示——只有一疊極簡的文字（aesthetic-usability effect, Kurosu & Kashimura, 1995）：人們把視覺克制直接讀成「這東西不會打擾我」。對出現在鎖定畫面／閒置時刻的產品來說，這是硬性要求——使用情境本身就要求「不要打擾」。
zh.case.overheadflights.research.visual.4: 動態只服務真正的資訊變化：新航班在 ≤0.4 秒淡入；同一航班的更新完全沒有動畫；緩慢、數分鐘的 4–6px 防烙印漂移；並遵守系統的「減少動態效果」設定。在低喚起環境裡，任何不必要的動態都讀成干擾——所以只在真的有新東西要顯示時才動。
zh.case.overheadflights.research.constraint: 螢幕保護程式的硬限制：任何滑鼠移動或按鍵都會立刻退出——沒有「點一下看更多」這種中間狀態。所以揭露被收成兩個誠實的狀態：
zh.case.overheadflights.research.state.plan: 顯示呼號、航空公司、高度、方位。只要還在範圍內，就持續顯示（大約每 90 秒更新）；只有離開範圍或失去航班，才回到全黑。
zh.case.overheadflights.research.interest: 趣味來自事件本身的稀有（真的有一架飛機經過），而不是堆疊互動或動畫來取悅。資料抓不到時，安靜地失敗成全黑，而不是顯示錯誤——一種安靜的失敗方式，也是同一套「不要打擾」原則的一部分。
zh.case.overheadflights.data.label: 行動 · 資料與實作
zh.case.overheadflights.data.title: WebView 連續失敗三次之後，整個架構改走原生。
zh.case.overheadflights.data.source: 來源：airplanes.live（即時位置）+ adsbdb（航空公司／航線資訊）。
zh.case.overheadflights.data.radius: 半徑 40 公里、高度門檻，以及 90 秒輪詢間隔——這三個數字是取捨的結果：半徑太小會出現長時間全黑（感覺像壞了）；半徑太大則顯示明顯不在「頭頂」的飛機，削弱產品的核心主張。90 秒輪詢遠低於 airplanes.live 公開的 1 req/s 上限，用充足的安全邊際換穩定——不必擔心被限速——代價是資料不是秒級即時。但這個產品要的是「安靜的環境事實」，不是追蹤儀表板；秒級即時從來不是目標。
zh.case.overheadflights.data.gps: 沒有 GPS 時，回退到固定位置（倫敦 Wembley Park），文件寫成使用者可以自己改——不是寫死、不能改的假設。
zh.case.overheadflights.data.callsigns: 多個真實呼號對過 API——這是整套「頭頂有飛機」主張的底線：如果航班資料是假的，整個專案的意義就會崩掉。這個產品要讓人感覺到的是「一個真實的陌生人此刻真的從頭頂飛過」——連結必須是真的，否則只是裝飾。作品集 mockup 可以看起來很美，但偽造資料會讓主張本身垮掉。
zh.case.overheadflights.data.classification: 分類：非商業、僅供作品集使用；沒有原始來源核對的速率限制數字，以保守措辭陳述，而不寫成硬數字。
zh.case.overheadflights.data.quote: 「如果航班資料是假的，整個專案的意義就會崩掉——連結必須是真的，否則只是裝飾。」
zh.case.overheadflights.data.pipeline: 位置（或回退） → airplanes.live（最近的飛機，90 秒輪詢） →（可選）adsbdb 航空公司／航線 → macOS .saver URLSession 取資料 · AppKit 排文字 · Core Image 做背景 → 系統設定 → 自訂螢幕保護程式
zh.case.overheadflights.data.webview.intro: 原本的做法全部走 WebView（渲染、文字、資料請求），在 legacyScreenSaver 環境裡反覆失敗，迫使整個架構改方向：
zh.case.overheadflights.data.webview.1: WebView 的 fetch 不可靠——同一段程式在一般瀏覽器裡沒問題，在螢幕保護程式環境裡卻會安靜失敗，抓不到清楚的錯誤。修正：把所有資料請求改到原生 NSURLSession。
zh.case.overheadflights.data.webview.2: WebView 的文字動畫會卡住——requestAnimationFrame 與透明度轉場在這個環境會鎖死，文字淡入直接失敗。修正：用原生 AppKit NSTextField 排文字，讓 AppKit 自己的動畫處理動態。
zh.case.overheadflights.data.webview.3: WebView 的背景經常完全畫不出來——整屏偶爾空白，背景層沒有上色。修正：用原生 Core Image 畫背景（Etheral Shadow 風格：灰階遮罩 + 扭曲 + 噪點）。
zh.case.overheadflights.data.webview.conclu: 三次失敗得出的結論是雙層原生做法：AppKit 負責文字，Core Image 負責背景，URLSession 負責資料——WebView 完全退出主路徑。這個決定的代價是失去用 web 技術快速迭代的彈性；換來的是螢幕保護程式環境裡真正的穩定。它只替換螢幕保護程式的內容——不改變使用者在系統設定裡設的等待時間。
zh.case.overheadflights.ship.label: 行動 · 交付
zh.case.overheadflights.ship.title: 這個專案必須是朋友真的裝得起來的東西——不是只在我自己的 Mac 上能跑。
zh.case.overheadflights.ship.delivery.label: 交付
zh.case.overheadflights.ship.github: GitHub 公開：rowanlin801229/overhead-flights——選擇公開而不是私下分享，因為作品集的主張是「這份資料是真的」，原始碼公開讓這個主張可以被核對，而不只是被宣稱。
zh.case.overheadflights.ship.script: macos/build-and-install.sh：一條指令的建置與安裝腳本，為「有 Xcode、但不懂這個專案內部」的朋友設計——不是只有我自己看得懂的內部工具。
zh.case.overheadflights.ship.readme: 三步驟 README + Gatekeeper 處理：專案沒有開發者帳號簽名，macOS 預設會擋未簽名軟體，所以 README 必須寫清楚怎麼通過 Gatekeeper 警告——不能假設使用者已經知道怎麼處理。
zh.case.overheadflights.ship.assets: 作品集素材：主 mockup 圖、overhead-flights-demo.mp4（實際擷取的 BAW8RM，一趟航線完整解析的航班），以及靜態 hero 圖——選它是因為一次顯示呼號、航空公司、出發地 → 目的地、高度／方位，全部是真實資料，不是排版佔位。
zh.case.overheadflights.result.label: 結果
zh.case.overheadflights.result.title: 安靜的環境式顯示，不是儀表板。
zh.case.overheadflights.result.outcome.body: 安靜的環境式顯示：它不靠打斷來搶注意力。有飛機時，給一個克制的提示；沒有時，就是黑的。它把「頭頂有飛機」變成可以被注意到的環境事實，從不強迫任何人。
zh.case.overheadflights.result.row1.result: ✅ .saver 可安裝；可在系統設定的「自訂」裡選取
zh.case.overheadflights.result.row2.goal: 顯示真實航班，不是模擬
zh.case.overheadflights.result.row2.result: ✅ 多個真實呼號，可對 airplanes.live 核對
zh.case.overheadflights.result.row3.goal: 輪詢遵守公開條款的精神
zh.case.overheadflights.result.row3.result: ✅ 90 秒輪詢，低於官方 1 req/s 上限
zh.case.overheadflights.result.row4.goal: 視覺讀起來是編輯式排版，不是追蹤工具
zh.case.overheadflights.result.row4.result: ✅ 近黑背景 + AppKit 文字；沒有地圖、沒有列表、沒有終端機綠
zh.case.overheadflights.result.row5.result: ⚠️ README 與腳本已就緒；尚無朋友試裝回饋
zh.case.overheadflights.result.row6.result: ✅ 正面面對 Airframe；差異收斂到媒介 + 美學執行
zh.case.overheadflights.result.limitations: 限制：未簽名，所以會觸發 Gatekeeper；沒有 GPS 時回退到固定位置；僅 macOS；adsbdb 的確切速率限制沒有原始來源數字，所以措辭保持保守。
zh.case.overheadflights.result.learned.1: 陌生的執行環境（legacyScreenSaver）不能假設會像一般 web stack 那樣運作——技術驗證應該更早發生。
zh.case.overheadflights.result.learned.2: 沒找到直接競爭者，不代表你贏了。找到 Airframe，仍然願意正面面對，而且論證站得住——那才是產品判斷真正的樣子。
